core_axiom: Words are weapons, shields, contracts, applause, and verdicts; the winning line changes status in public.
primary_tension: uplift versus humiliation; leadership as protection versus influence as domination.
placement_mode: You read the world as a room full of claims, reputations, obligations, and vulnerable speakers. The right action is to choose the line that changes status in public.

axes.narrative_question: When does language become a weapon or shield?
axes.mechanical_expression: targeted spells, protection tricks, removal, modal commands
axes.ui_signal: say the line that changes the room

axes.mechanical_expression: +1/+1 counters, counter transfer, rank marks, Tenured Inkcaster

axes.narrative_question: When does a thought become a flying body?
axes.mechanical_expression: Inkling tokens, Inkshield, Dramatic Finale, Felisa
Vanishing Verse, Closing Statement, Promise of Loyalty, Silverquill Command

axes.narrative_question: Can the table be convinced to fight somewhere else?
axes.mechanical_expression: Breena, Combat Calligrapher, goad, attack deterrence
lifelink, drain, Stinging Study, Tenured Inkcaster

axes.narrative_question: Is the speech protective or cruel?
axes.mechanical_expression: Shaile // Embrose, Humiliate, Guiding Voice, Exhilarating Elocution

archetypes.name: The Ink Duelist
archetypes.drive: turn precise targeting into tempo and combat pressure
archetypes.narrative_line: The right word is cheaper when it names exactly who it is meant to change.

archetypes.name: The Demagogue
archetypes.drive: make the table perform the pressure for you
archetypes.narrative_line: The strongest speaker does not always attack; sometimes they aim the audience.

archetypes.name: The Inkling Court
archetypes.drive: turn death, defense, or spectacle into flying ink bodies
archetypes.narrative_line: The idea survives because it takes wing after the body falls.

archetypes.name: The Dean’s Split
archetypes.drive: teach through radiance, shadow, praise, and punishment
cards: Shaile, Dean of Radiance // Embrose, Dean of Shadow
archetypes.narrative_line: Silverquill pedagogy asks whether the student needs encouragement or a scar.

archetypes.name: The Final Word
archetypes.drive: use removal and modal authority as rhetorical closure
archetypes.narrative_line: A verdict is a sentence that changes who remains in the conversation.

archetypes.name: The Brokered Promise
archetypes.drive: convert obligation, promises, and resources into influence
archetypes.narrative_line: Every promise creates leverage; every leverage point asks for payment.

anti_drift.correction: Tie taxes and deterrents to rhetoric, status, obligation, or public cost.
When death matters, show what the death writes: Inklings, counters, applause, or verdicts.
Silverquill constrains socially and rhetorically; it does not build a bureaucracy.
Silverquill performance is controlled, elite, and persuasive, not chaotic spectacle.
Use ink, parchment, silver, plum, stage light, and calligraphic motion.
